kind: semantic follow-up; not a winning replay or complete impossibility proof
claims: The directed static model leaves a nine-cell final pocket after gateway (24,0) is removed. Ordinary movement cannot leave it by a lower-board path: the remaining boundaries are permanent walls, board edges or north-facing thin walls.

A stationary block at (24,0) cannot be removed from inside the final pocket: its north move leaves the board, its west push requires Chip at (25,0), its east push requires Chip at (23,0), and its south push requires Chip outside the board.
The native thin-wall leave check happens before pushblock, so a mouse goal from row 1 cannot perform a perpendicular slap on an ice block in row 0.
The only teleports are (11,0) and (25,4); teleport-push exemptions cannot act on any final-gate ice cell.

Before the final chip is collected, optimistic ordinary-monster reachability excludes the listed gate cells and both teleports under the assumptions in 723-monster-cut.json. Both cloners produce blocks only.

For blocks confined to the straight ice cells (25..27,0), blocks to the right of the leftmost block do not obstruct its westward exit while (24,0) is empty; they can cause earlier reversal. This local collision observation does not bound scheduler delay. Occupying (24,0) itself closes the gateway.

distinctLocalProbe.description: Follow pushed block onto ice25,0, bounce safely back to24,0, then attempt outward-and-return corridor route; alters Chip slip participation.
distinctLocalProbe.observationNote: Recorded exploratory run; elapsed time and cutoff-limited trial counts vary across machines. Runner preserves the bounded strategy and exact prefix, not identical wall-clock metrics.

remainingLoophole: No bound or construction covers every attainable global slipper configuration, including helper-created persistent oscillators, mixed normal/reversing predecessors, altered clone-corridor occupancy, forced-ice departures or legitimate mouse timing. Return on later block cycles also remains part of the unresolved reachability question. Count-only or logarithmic index-contraction bounds are not established: a reversing immediate predecessor can shift the gate left by only one list index and skip it. These local constraints do not establish impossibility.
scope: Original level; static geometry and source inspection supplement the native-verified partial route. Not a complete impossibility proof.

assumptions: Start with a fresh ordinary east push from (23,0) into (24,0), setting Chip HASMOVED.
Use the ordinary corridor out to (31,0) and back to (24,0), with no intervening forced-ice excursion, movement-state reset or other shortcut.
Choose the most favorable push phase, allowing the first south move one tick later; the remaining seventeen ordinary moves are four ticks apart.
freshPushTiming.limitation: This is a conditional fresh-push route bound, not a universal return-time bound. An ice excursion can change Chip movement state and requires separate timing analysis.

mouseScope: The source checks rule out the stated geometric perpendicular push, including mouse goals. They do not rule out every timing effect of legitimate absolute mouse retargeting elsewhere.
